title: Zephyrine and the Deadline
premise: Hazel Reyes, a fixer for the Meridian Office — an embassy that exists on no map and in no treaty — discovers the safe house where she once trained has been listed for sale online, its interior photographed down to the bullet-scarred doorframe. Someone inside her own agency is liquidating the evidence of the program that broke her and killed her partner, Elias. As Hazel hunts the seller through a chain of brokers, defectors, and one very dangerous archivist, she assembles a ragtag crew of other program survivors who become the family she never had. In the end she chooses love over duty, burning the network's records and her own career with them, and finally sleeps through the night.
about_author: Paloma Galloway is a former diplomatic courier who spent a decade crossing borders with sealed pouches and unasked questions. She writes thrillers from a farmhouse in the Azores, where the nearest embassy is a ferry ride away.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Scrolling a real estate site at 3 a.m., she recognizes the safe house from her training days — every scar in the walls photographed like a feature. She reports it to the Office and is told to stand down. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into defiance as she realizes the agency wants the past erased, not investigated.

chapters.title: Chain of Custody
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Working off the books, she traces the listing to a broker in Trieste who deals only in 'sanitized' properties. The broker recognizes her file photo and panics, leaving a burner number behind. Emotional beat: the thrill of competence curdling as she understands she's being tracked by someone who knows her tradecraft.

chapters.title: The Archivist
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Hazel and Wren, a former program records clerk living under three names. Wren confirms the Office ran a 'disposal protocol' — selling safe houses after burning their paper trails, and the people in them. Emotional beat: two lonely professionals recognizing each other, the first fragile thread of found family.

chapters.title: What Elias Knew
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, with flashbacks. She reopens the file on her partner's death, finding his last report flagged by the same office now selling the safe houses. A surveillance team burns her apartment; she escapes with nothing but a go-bag and Elias's notebook. Emotional beat: grief transmuting into purpose.

chapters.title: Crew of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren and Hazel gather survivors: Dez, a handler turned bartender; Ines, the program's former medic; and Tomas, a teenager the program never finished training. Hiding in a decommissioned lighthouse, they map the disposal network. Emotional beat: cautious warmth — strangers becoming a unit, a family assembling itself.

chapters.title: The Buyer
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The trail leads to Calloway Voss, a private intelligence magnate buying the safe houses to reconstruct the program for his own clients. He offers Hazel a partnership: her skills for Elias's full file. Emotional beat: temptation — power dangled as a cure for grief, and the horror of realizing she almost wants it.

chapters.title: Insider
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The crew discovers a leak: someone sold their location to the Office's internal security arm. A near-fatal raid on the lighthouse forces the crew to scatter, and Ines is taken. Emotional beat: betrayal and guilt — the found family's first fracture, and Tomas's desperate need to prove he belongs.

chapters.title: The Auction
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, infiltrating Voss's estate where the final safe house — and the program's master archive — will be sold to the highest bidder. She trades herself to Voss to buy the crew time, learning Elias died protecting the archive's location. Emotional beat: love against duty — she surrenders her freedom to protect people, not country.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Crew POV, ensemble. Dez, Wren, and Tomas run a coordinated op: rescue Ines, breach the archive vault, and ignite the thermite Hazel smuggled in. Voss dies protecting his purchase; the Office's complicity is broadcast before the servers melt. Emotional beat: the climax — chaos, sacrifice, and the family holding together under fire.

chapters.title: Sleep
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, epilogue. The crew disperses to new names, promising one dinner a year. Hazel, officially erased and finally free, visits Elias's grave and hands his notebook to a journalist. That night, in a rented room with no safe house features at all, she sleeps until morning. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — grief integrated, family chosen, the deadline met.
